angle: Explanation forms beyond feature attribution + self-explaining models, applied to network traffic classification / NIDS where possible

papers.title: AI/ML for Network Security: The Emperor has no Clothes (Trustee)
papers.authors: Arthur S. Jacobs, Roman Beltiukov, Walter Willinger, Ronaldo A. Ferreira, Arpit Gupta
papers.relevance: The central decision-tree-surrogate paper for network security: extracts high-fidelity, low-complexity, stable decision trees plus a 'trust report' from any black-box network-ML model, and uses them to expose shortcut learning, spurious correlations, and o.o.d. vulnerability in published NIDS models.

papers.title: Interpreting Deep Learning-Based Networking Systems (Metis)
papers.authors: Zili Meng, Minhu Wang, Jiasong Bai, et al.
papers.relevance: First systematic surrogate-model framework for DL-based networking systems: converts local-system DNN policies to interpretable rule/decision-tree forms and graph-based systems to hypergraph explanations, enabling operators to debug, deploy, and lighten networking DNNs.

papers.title: xNIDS: Explaining Deep Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems for Active Intrusion Responses
papers.authors: Feng Wei, Hongda Li, Ziming Zhao, Hongxin Hu
papers.relevance: Moves NIDS explanation output beyond saliency to ACTIONABLE DEFENSE RULES (entity/action/priority/timeout translated to OpenFlow, iptables, pfSense, Squid), arguing prior explainers lack the fidelity, sparsity, completeness and stability needed for active response.

papers.title: DeepAID: Interpreting and Improving Deep Learning-based Anomaly Detection in Security Applications
papers.authors: Dongqi Han, Zhiliang Wang, Wenqi Chen, et al.
papers.relevance: Reference-based (counterfactual-flavored) interpretation for UNSUPERVISED security anomaly detectors: searches a nearby in-distribution 'normal' reference for each anomaly and distills the detector into an interpretable finite-state model (Distiller), covering network intrusion among its use cases.

papers.title: CADE: Detecting and Explaining Concept Drift Samples for Security Applications
papers.authors: Limin Yang, Wenbo Guo, Qingying Hao, Arridhana Ciptadi, Ali Ahmadzadeh, Xinyu Xing, Gang Wang
papers.relevance: Contrastive, distance-based explanation (not attribution over a decision boundary) for drifting samples, with the authors' own finding that explaining 'distance' beats explaining 'a decision boundary'; case studies include network intrusion detection.

papers.title: DeepCASE: Semi-Supervised Contextual Analysis of Security Events
papers.authors: Thijs van Ede, Hojjat Aghakhani, Noah Spahn, et al.
papers.relevance: Case-based-style interpretability for security event streams: attention over event context plus clustering of correlated sequences so analysts label a handful of representative 'cases' instead of millions of events, reducing manual inspection workload by ~95%.

papers.title: Genos: General In-Network Unsupervised Intrusion Detection by Rule Extraction
papers.authors: Ruoyu Li, Qing Li, Yu Zhang, et al.
papers.relevance: Rule extraction from unsupervised anomaly detectors via divide-and-conquer feature-space partitioning so the surrogate rules run IN the data plane at '100 Gbps throughput, great interpretability, and trivial updating overhead' -- rule extraction as both explanation and deployment vehicle.

papers.title: Traffic-CBM: A Structurally Interpretable Multimodal Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.authors: Honglei Jin, Wenshuo Chen, Shaofeng Liang, et al.
papers.relevance: The FIRST concept-bottleneck-style model for encrypted traffic classification (mid-2026 preprint): organizes heterogeneous traffic signals into an explicit hierarchical concept representation, giving 'a clearer structural explanation of multimodal traffic evidence' at competitive accuracy -- evidence that CBMs on traffic are brand-new territory.

papers.title: Novel Actionable Counterfactual Explanations for Intrusion Detection Using Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Vinura Galwaduge, Jagath Samarabandu
papers.relevance: Tabular-diffusion counterfactual generator for DL-NIDS that produces 'minimal, diverse counterfactual explanations' and converts them into actionable security rules (same group's arXiv:2507.17161 preprint 'Tabular Diffusion based Actionable Counterfactual Explanations for Network Intrusion Detection' is included as the open PDF).

papers.title: Explaining AI-Informed Network Intrusion Detection with Counterfactuals
papers.authors: (retrieved via OpenAlex; IEEE INFOCOM Workshops)
papers.relevance: Early direct application of counterfactual explanation to AI-based NIDS decisions, one of only a handful of pre-2025 counterfactual-NIDS papers.

papers.title: ProvX: Generating Counterfactual-Driven Attack Explanations for Provenance-Based Detection
papers.authors: Weiheng Wu, Wei Qiao, Teng Li, et al.
papers.relevance: Counterfactual explanation for GNN-based provenance/attack detection: relaxes the discrete graph-perturbation search 'into a continuous optimization task' to find minimal structures whose removal flips the detection -- the graph-counterfactual recipe transferable to flow-graph NIDS.

papers.title: Two-Stage Intrusion Detection System in Intelligent Transportation Systems Using Rule Extraction Methods From Deep Neural Networks
papers.authors: (IEEE T-ITS; retrieved via OpenAlex)
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
papers.relevance: Applies classic pedagogical rule-extraction from trained DNNs to vehicular/ITS network intrusion detection, one of the most-cited direct 'rule extraction on NIDS' studies.

papers.title: Achieving Explainability of Intrusion Detection System by Hybrid Oracle-Explainer Approach
papers.authors: (IJCNN 2020; retrieved via OpenAlex)
papers.relevance: Pairs a black-box 'oracle' NIDS with a co-trained interpretable explainer model (surrogate architecture), an early template for self-explaining-by-construction intrusion detection.

papers.title: Explainable Boosting Machines for Network Intrusion Detection with Features Reduction
papers.authors: (Springer LNCS; retrieved via OpenAlex)
papers.relevance: Interpretable-by-design glass-box (EBM/GAM family) applied to NIDS, showing additive shape-function models can rival black-box accuracy while being globally inspectable.

papers.title: A soft prototype-based autonomous fuzzy inference system for network intrusion detection
papers.authors: (Information Sciences; retrieved via OpenAlex)
papers.relevance: Prototype-based, self-organizing fuzzy rule system for NIDS -- the closest existing thing to prototype-style interpretability actually deployed on traffic (via fuzzy prototypes rather than ProtoPNet-style learned prototypes).

papers.title: From evidence to decision: Concept-prototype reasoning for intrusion detection in SDN-based industrial networks
papers.authors: (Computer Networks; retrieved via OpenAlex)
papers.relevance: Very recent combination of concept-level and prototype-level reasoning for SDN/IIoT intrusion detection -- together with Traffic-CBM it marks the 2026 arrival of concept/prototype explanation forms in networking.

papers.title: A Synergistic Approach In Network Intrusion Detection By Neurosymbolic AI
papers.authors: Alice Bizzarri, Chung-En Yu, Brian Jalaian, et al.
papers.relevance: Integrates symbolic logic reasoning with deep NIDS to address 'computational demands and interpretability challenges' -- a working neurosymbolic NIDS whose explanations are logic-form rather than attribution.

papers.title: Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence for Robust Network Intrusion Detection: From Scratch to Transfer Learning (ODXU)
papers.authors: Huynh T. T. Tran, Jacob Sander, Achraf Cohen, et al.
papers.relevance: Neurosymbolic NIDS framework (deep feature extraction + symbolic reasoning + uncertainty quantification) shown to beat pure neural models especially under limited training data; companion transfer-learning study is arXiv:2509.10850.

papers.title: Interpretable Sequence Classification via Discrete Optimization
papers.authors: Maayan Shvo, Andrew C. Li, Rodrigo Toro Icarte, Sheila A. McIlraith
papers.relevance: Learns automata-based, interpretable-by-design sequence classifiers that natively support counterfactual reasoning and match LSTM accuracy, explicitly motivated by intrusion-detection-style early classification -- a self-explaining model family barely explored on real traffic.

papers.title: Explainable Malware Detection with Tailored Logic Explained Networks
papers.authors: Peter Anthony, Francesco Giannini, Michelangelo Diligenti, et al.
papers.relevance: Adapts Logic Explained Networks to malware detection on EMBER, producing first-order-logic explanations at black-box-level accuracy -- proves LENs work in security, but on malware binaries, NOT on network traffic.

papers.title: CrystalBox: Future-Based Explanations for Input-Driven Deep RL Systems
papers.authors: Sagar Patel, Sangeetha Abdu Jyothi, Nina Narodytska
papers.relevance: A genuinely different explanation form for networking ML -- decomposed FUTURE REWARD explanations for deep-RL controllers (adaptive bitrate, congestion control) instead of input attribution; networking control rather than traffic classification.

papers.title: Case-based reasoning for intrusion detection
papers.authors: M. Esmaili et al.
papers.relevance: Seminal pre-DL application of case-based reasoning to intrusion detection -- the historical anchor showing CBR-for-IDS existed, though its explanation-by-precedent framing has never been revisited with modern neural retrieval.

papers.title: A Multi-agent Case-Based Reasoning Intrusion Detection System Prototype
papers.authors: (Springer LNCS; retrieved via OpenAlex)
papers.relevance: Recent CBR-based IDS prototype confirming the case-based line is still alive but marginal -- explanation-by-similar-past-incident remains essentially unexplored against deep NIDS baselines.

papers.title: Neuro-Symbolic AI for Cybersecurity: State of the Art, Challenges, and Opportunities
papers.authors: Safayat Bin Hakim, Muhammad Adil, Alvaro Velasquez, et al.
papers.relevance: Systematic review of 103 neurosymbolic-security publications -- the map of which symbolic-reasoning explanation forms have and have not reached network defense.

papers.title: DriftTrace: Combating Concept Drift in Security Applications Through Detection and Explanation
papers.authors: (IEEE TIFS; retrieved via OpenAlex)
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
papers.relevance: CADE-successor line: joint drift detection plus explanation for security models, continuing the distance/reference-based explanation form.

papers.title: PacketCLIP: Multi-Modal Embedding of Network Traffic and Language for Cybersecurity Reasoning
papers.authors: Ryozo Masukawa, Sanggeon Yun, Sungheon Jeong, et al.
papers.relevance: Contrastive packet-plus-natural-language embedding with GNN-based hierarchical reasoning, pitching language-grounded 'interpretable' traffic analysis -- a semantic/concept-adjacent explanation form for encrypted traffic.

papers.title: Treat Traffic Like Trees: A Semantic-Preserving Hierarchical Graph-Based Expert Framework for Encrypted Traffic Analysis (PTGAMoE)
papers.authors: Yuantu Luo, Jun Tao, Linxiao Yu, et al.
papers.relevance: Interpretable-by-structure mixture-of-experts over protocol-field graphs whose expert committees reveal 'model's preferences for specific fields and protocols' -- structural self-explanation for encrypted traffic.

papers.title: Hybrid Shaping with LIME and Counterfactual Explanations (DiCE) for Explainable AI in Intrusion Detection Systems
papers.authors: (IEEE AMCAI; retrieved via OpenAlex)
papers.relevance: Directly plugs the off-the-shelf DiCE counterfactual generator (paired with LIME) into an IDS pipeline -- representative of the small 2024-2025 wave applying tabular-counterfactual tooling to NIDS features.

papers.title: Counterfactual Explanations without Opening the Black Box: Automated Decisions and the GDPR
papers.authors: Sandra Wachter, Brent Mittelstadt, Chris Russell
papers.relevance: The founding counterfactual-explanation paper ('smallest change to the world' that flips the decision) that every counterfactual-NIDS work builds on.

papers.title: Actionable Recourse in Linear Classification
papers.authors: Berk Ustun, Alexander Spangher, Yang Liu
papers.relevance: Defines actionable recourse with integer-programming feasibility/mutability constraints -- the formal recourse machinery that NO retrieved paper has yet transplanted to flow-feature space (where 'actionability' means enforceable network rules).

papers.title: Explaining Machine Learning Classifiers through Diverse Counterfactual Explanations (DiCE)
papers.authors: Ramaravind K. Mothilal, Amit Sharma, Chenhao Tan
papers.relevance: The diversity-plus-feasibility counterfactual generator (DPP-based) that the 2024-2025 IDS counterfactual papers actually import.

papers.title: Counterfactual explanations and how to find them: literature review and benchmarking
papers.authors: Riccardo Guidotti
papers.relevance: The standard survey/benchmark of tabular counterfactual explainers -- the menu of methods still untested on traffic features.

papers.title: A Survey of Algorithmic Recourse: Contrastive Explanations and Consequential Recommendations
papers.authors: Amir-Hossein Karimi, Gilles Barthe, Bernhard Schoelkopf, Isabel Valera
papers.relevance: Canonical recourse survey separating contrastive explanation from consequential recommendation -- the conceptual frame for turning NIDS counterfactuals into operator actions.

papers.title: Interpretability Beyond Feature Attribution: Quantitative Testing with Concept Activation Vectors (TCAV)
papers.authors: Been Kim, Martin Wattenberg, Justin Gilmer, et al.
papers.relevance: THE 'beyond feature attribution' paper: tests concept importance via directional derivatives (CAVs); across all searches, no application of TCAV to network traffic classification was found.

papers.title: Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.authors: Pang Wei Koh, Thao Nguyen, Yew Siang Tang, et al.
papers.relevance: Foundational CBM paper with test-time concept intervention; the CBM family reached traffic only in mid-2026 (Traffic-CBM), so interventions, probabilistic/editable/post-hoc CBM variants remain untried on traffic.

papers.title: Do Concept Bottleneck Models Learn as Intended?
papers.authors: Andrei Margeloiu, Matthew Ashman, Umang Bhatt, et al.
papers.relevance: Key CBM critique -- learned concepts may not map to meaningful input features -- a validity threat any traffic-CBM must answer (what IS a human concept for an encrypted flow?).

papers.title: This Looks Like That: Deep Learning for Interpretable Image Recognition (ProtoPNet)
papers.authors: Chaofan Chen, Oscar Li, Chaofan Tao, et al.
papers.relevance: The prototype-part self-explaining architecture; no ProtoPNet-style model over packet/flow representations surfaced in any search -- an open transfer.

papers.title: Towards Robust Interpretability with Self-Explaining Neural Networks (SENN)
papers.authors: David Alvarez-Melis, Tommi S. Jaakkola
papers.relevance: Defines self-explaining models via explicitness/faithfulness/stability constraints trained in; no SENN-style architecture for traffic classification was found.

papers.title: Interpretable and Steerable Sequence Learning via Prototypes (ProSeNet)
papers.authors: Yao Ming, Panpan Xu, Huamin Qu, Liu Ren
papers.relevance: Prototype-based self-explaining SEQUENCE model with human steering -- a natural but untried fit for packet/flow sequences (no traffic application retrieved).

papers.title: Distilling a Neural Network Into a Soft Decision Tree
papers.authors: Nicholas Frosst, Geoffrey Hinton
papers.relevance: Soft-decision-tree distillation of DNNs; network security surrogate work (Trustee, Metis, Genos) uses HARD trees, so soft-tree distillation of NIDS models remains untried.

papers.title: Extracting Tree-Structured Representations of Trained Networks (TREPAN)
papers.authors: Mark W. Craven, Jude W. Shavlik
papers.relevance: The original pedagogical rule/tree-extraction algorithm that Trustee explicitly modernizes for network-ML models -- the root of the surrogate-tree lineage.

papers.title: Anchors: High-Precision Model-Agnostic Explanations
papers.authors: Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Sameer Singh, Carlos Guestrin
papers.relevance: Rule-form local explanations (IF-THEN anchors with precision guarantees); appears in XAI-IDS comparison studies but no dedicated anchors-for-traffic study surfaced.

papers.title: Logic Explained Networks
papers.authors: Gabriele Ciravegna, Pietro Barbiero, Francesco Giannini, et al.
papers.relevance: Self-explaining architecture emitting first-order-logic explanations; applied to malware (2024) but NEVER to network traffic classification in any retrieved result.

papers.title: Stop Explaining Black Box Machine Learning Models for High Stakes Decisions and Use Interpretable Models Instead
papers.authors: Cynthia Rudin
papers.relevance: The interpretable-by-design manifesto ('explaining black boxes is likely to perpetuate bad practices') that frames the whole self-explaining-NIDS agenda.

papers.title: SoK: Explainable Machine Learning for Computer Security Applications
papers.authors: Azqa Nadeem, Daniel Vos, Clinton Cao, et al.
papers.relevance: Systematization of XAI-in-security by stakeholder/goal; documents that 'user studies accompany only 14% of XAI security applications' and pushes interpretability-by-design -- the gap map this corpus fills.

papers.title: Neurosymbolic AI Transfer Learning Improves Network Intrusion Detection
papers.authors: Huynh T. T. Tran, Jacob Sander, Achraf Cohen, et al.
papers.relevance: Follow-on to ODXU showing neurosymbolic NIDS pre-trained on large datasets transfers to small-sample settings better than pure neural models.

never_tried_on_network_traffic: TCAV / concept activation vector testing (no traffic application found in any query; existing CAV work is images, music, emotion, LLMs)
Formal actionable recourse (Ustun-style feasibility/immutability-constrained optimization) over flow features -- 2025 diffusion papers borrow the word 'actionable' but not the formalism
ProtoPNet-style part-prototype architectures and ProSeNet-style sequence prototypes on packet/flow data (closest existing: fuzzy soft prototypes, Inf. Sci. 2024; concept-prototype SDN, ComNet 2026)
Logic Explained Networks on traffic/NIDS (only malware/EMBER as of 2024)
SENN self-explaining regularization for traffic classifiers
Soft decision tree distillation (Frosst-Hinton) of NIDS models -- all networking surrogates retrieved use hard trees/rules

Concept bottleneck INTERVENTIONS (test-time concept editing) on traffic -- Traffic-CBM (2026) builds the bottleneck but the CBM-variant literature (probabilistic, editable, post-hoc CBMs) is untouched for traffic
Modern neural case-based-reasoning explanation (twin systems / precedent retrieval) for NIDS -- CBR-IDS literature is pre-deep-learning (1996-2005) plus one 2023 prototype
notes: RECURRING DATASETS: legacy KDD99/NSL-KDD-era and UNSW-NB15-style tabular IDS benchmarks dominate the surrounding IDS literature returned by every query; CADE evaluates on Android malware + network intrusion case studies; LEN-malware uses EMBER; Trustee re-audits published network-security models (its authors emphasize testing models 'published in the existing networking and network security literature'); the 2026 traffic papers (Traffic-CBM, PTGAMoE) target encrypted-traffic benchmarks. RECURRING EXPLANATION METHODS: (1) decision-tree/rule surrogate extraction is the dominant beyond-attribution form in networking (TREPAN -> Trustee, Metis, Genos, T-ITS two-stage, IJCNN oracle-explainer); (2) counterfactuals arrived late (2023 INFOCOM-W) and got serious only in 2025 via diffusion generators and DiCE imports; (3) reference/distance-based explanation is a security-native form (DeepAID's in-distribution reference search; CADE explaining 'distance' rather than 'a decision boundary'; DriftTrace); (4) explanation-to-action pipelines are a networking specialty: xNIDS and the diffusion-counterfactual papers both compile explanations into enforceable rules (OpenFlow/iptables), and Genos runs extracted rules in the data plane at '100 Gbps throughput'; (5) neurosymbolic NIDS is an active 2024-2025 cluster (Bizzarri; Tran/ODXU; 103-paper survey). RECURRING MODELS BEING EXPLAINED: autoencoder/unsupervised anomaly detectors (DeepAID, Genos), RNN/LSTM sequence detectors (DeepCASE, xNIDS targets stateful DL-NIDS), GNNs (ProvX provenance graphs, PacketCLIP), DRL controllers (Metis, CrystalBox), multimodal transformer traffic classifiers (Traffic-CBM, PTGAMoE). AUTHOR-STATED LIMITATIONS / FUTURE WORK seen in retrieved text: Trustee's authors state published network-ML models suffer 'shortcut learning, spurious correlations, and vulnerability to out-of-distribution samples' (underspecification the trees expose); xNIDS authors argue prior explanation methods are insufficient in 'fidelity, sparsity, completeness, and stability' for active intrusion response; CADE's authors report decision-boundary-style explanation fails for drift and 'explaining distance is much more effective'; Nadeem et al.'s SoK reports 'user studies accompany only 14% of XAI security applications' and flags interpretability-by-design as underused; Rudin warns post-hoc explanation of black boxes 'is likely to perpetuate bad practices' in high stakes; Margeloiu et al. show CBM concepts 'may not map to meaningful input features' -- a direct threat to porting CBMs to traffic where human concepts are undefined; the CAV literature itself reports method fragility (CAV sampling variability shrinking only as 1/N, arXiv:2509.24058; adversarial attacks on CAVs, arXiv:2509.22755) -- relevant caveats before proposing TCAV-for-traffic; Bizzarri et al. motivate neurosymbolic NIDS by the 'computational demands and interpretability challenges' of deep NIDS; Tran et al. show pure neural NIDS degrade with limited training samples, positioning symbolic components as the fix. GAP SUMMARY: rule/tree surrogates are mature for networks; counterfactuals are emerging (2023-2025); concept-, prototype-, logic-, and recourse-based forms are essentially virgin territory on traffic, with the first concept-flavored traffic papers appearing only in 2026.
